title: Optimize quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion, KV-cache scheduling & continuous batching
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token cost and latency for quantized model serving by improving INT8/FP8 kernel throughput and eliminating unnecessary dequant/quant roundtrips. This PR implements three complementary changes: (1) fusion-aware kernels that combine smoothquant scaling with dequantization to avoid an extra memory pass, (2) micro-optimized GEMM paths for INT8/FP8 that prefer vectorized layouts on Ampere/Next-gen GPUs, and (3) scheduler+KV-cache integration to allow continuous batching to co-schedule KV-cache warms with the first token of a sequence. The net effect is lower kernel latency and higher sustained throughput for common LLM workloads.

What changed (high level):
- Implemented SmoothQuant+Dequant fusion kernel (+path selector) that applies channel scaling during dequant step and writes directly to the runtime's preferred FP32/FP16 work buffer to avoid a separate re-quant pass.
- Added INT8/FP8 specialized GEMM kernels with layout fallback and improved memory prefetching for common sequence lengths (1, 8, 32, 128). Uses warp-level intrinsics where available.
- Extended the runtime scheduler to consider KV-cache warm-up cost: for short sequences we now opportunistically batch the first token(s) with pending KV-cache warms to reduce cold-start latency.
- Added a heuristics toggle (quant_fusion_enable) and an adaptive threshold based on measured bandwidth/compute to avoid regressions on older GPU types.
- Bench harness updates and microbench tests to measure per-op latency and end-to-end token latency across sequence length distributions.

Benchmarks (internal perf harness):
- Llama-2-13B int8/FP8 profile, seq=32, batch=8: 18% P95 token latency reduction, 12% throughput increase.
- GPT-style 70B int8, seq=128, batch=1: 11% latency reduction on Ampere, negligible change on older T4-class GPUs (guarded by threshold toggle).
- Continuous batching + KV-cache heuristic: tail latency P99 reduced by 22% on chat workload trace with many short turns.

Compatibility & safety:
- Feature guarded behind runtime flag and per-device capability check.
- Added extensive unit tests validating numerical error bounds (max relative error vs FP32 baseline) and operator fallback tests for devices without required intrinsics.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation
- [x] Scheduler integration
- [x] Microbench harness + data
- [x] Unit tests + numerical tolerances
- [x] Docs comment and feature flag

Notes:
- This PR focuses on inference-time fusion; training paths are not affected.
- We observed a small (<=0.5%) accuracy drift for aggressive fusion on a tiny subset of examples; default thresholds are conservative. See bench/notes/915123 for the raw traces.

References: ENG-1426 (quant performance epic), ENG-1480 (kvcache cold-start work), related PRs: pr-821456, pr-118234 for prior scheduling work.
